guidance.when: An operative return-or-destruction duty is directly triggered by termination, expiration, rejection, conclusion, ceasing interest, completion, abandonment, a transaction closing, or another ending of the covered agreement, project, evaluation, discussions, or relationship.
guidance.inspection: Match the duty and ending event in the same provision or an explicit cross-reference. A request-only duty, a survival clause, a restriction period, or an agreement effective date does not supply the trigger. Delivery at a transaction's effective closing qualifies only when that closing ends the covered relationship and the delivery duty applies to confidential material.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the actor-bearing duty, the exact ending-event language, and every operative return or destruction branch; exclude request-only, survival, duration, and unrelated effective-date text.

guidance.when: A return or destruction regime expressly exempts archival backups, inaccessible system copies, or a retained legal or compliance copy.
guidance.inspection: Confirm that the receiving party may keep the specified confidential information despite the otherwise applicable return or destruction duty, and preserve limitations on access, purpose, duration, and continuing confidentiality.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the exception or override language, every independently operative retention branch, and the conditions governing each retained category.

guidance.when: An applicable clause mandates return or destruction of all Confidential Information and all copies, without an operative retention exception.
guidance.inspection: Match the receiving actor, mandatory polarity, and universal protected object. The trigger may be a request, termination, or another stated event: trigger type does not prevent the clause from opposing retention. Do not infer exhaustive coverage from duties limited to documents, tangible items, particular media, or other subsets of Confidential Information.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the complete trigger and every branch establishing return or destruction of all Confidential Information and copies, plus any incorporated exception; do not cite survival or subset-only provisions.

guidance.when: An operative clause permits or necessarily authorizes creation of copies for a stated purpose, disclosure route, performance need, or automatic backup process.
guidance.inspection: Treat an immediate exception such as copying as necessary, required, or permitted for the contractual purpose as an affirmative copy route even when embedded in a prohibition. A rule saying only that copying requires future consent or approval is not present permission, and retention of pre-existing copies is not copy creation.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the actor-bearing chapeau and the complete copy exception or automatic-copy provision, including its purpose conditions; exclude consent-only prohibitions and retention-only clauses.

guidance.when: The receiving party is prohibited from reproducing or copying Confidential Information, including a prohibition stated as applying without prior written approval or consent, and no present operative copy exception applies.
guidance.inspection: Match actor, copied object, and prohibitory polarity. A possible future approval is not an existing permission. An employee-disclosure exception, retention of existing copies, or permitted use does not authorize creating copies unless the text expressly says so.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the actor-bearing chapeau, full no-copy branch, and any proviso needed to determine whether it concerns copying or only a different action.

guidance.when: An operative disclosure rule identifies employees, internal personnel, representatives, advisers, agents, consultants, contractors, or another recipient class, or prohibits disclosure to every person without an applicable class exception.
guidance.inspection: Resolve the recipient class and conditions separately for each hypothesis. Internal staff or employees support employee sharing; consultants, professional advisers, contractors, or external agents support third-party sharing. A blanket prohibition without a present class exception contradicts sharing with either requested class. An employee-only exception does not permit external sharing, and an external-only class does not automatically establish employee sharing.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the operative permission or prohibition, every definition needed to identify the class, and all need-to-know, purpose, consent, and confidentiality conditions.

guidance.when: The operative confidential-information definition expressly enumerates business, financial, marketing, customer, personnel, operational, regulatory, contact, or another non-technical subject category.
guidance.inspection: Require an affirmative non-technical subject category inside the operative definition or incorporated continuation. Do not rely on recitals, transaction background, generic references to all information or a submission, communication form, or recipient-created notes merely because they could contain non-technical material.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the definitional chapeau and every continuation needed to connect the expressly named non-technical category to Confidential Information; omit background descriptions and generic derived-material clauses.

guidance.when: The operative definition makes identification or marking by the disclosing party a necessary condition for every covered form of confidential disclosure.
guidance.inspection: Test every definitional route, including oral and electronic disclosures and any later written-confirmation process. This condition establishes entailment only when universal. Failure to find a universal marking condition does not itself establish contradiction; absent an affirmative non-identification route, the result remains unresolved.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include all clauses collectively covering every disclosure form and each required identification or confirmation step.

guidance.when: An operative definition expressly provides a sufficient alternative to disclosing-party identification, such as information being confidential because of its nature, surrounding circumstances, or a stated reasonable-recipient standard.
guidance.inspection: Confirm that the alternative is an eligibility rule that independently makes information confidential without identification. Do not infer such a route merely from broad coverage, information being furnished or deemed confidential, absence of marking language, examples of covered material, or a general care obligation.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the complete operative definition containing the affirmative alternative and only the text needed to show that it independently confers confidential status.

guidance.when: The definition or an identification procedure expressly covers information disclosed orally or verbally.
guidance.inspection: Confirm that oral communication is a covered disclosure form, including any condition requiring contemporaneous identification or later written confirmation. Broad coverage of information types without an oral modality does not suffice.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the definition or governing chapeau and the oral-disclosure branch, including any condition that makes the oral material confidential.

guidance.when: An operative duty prohibits disclosure or public announcement of the agreement's existence, negotiations or discussions, a prospective transaction, or transactions contemplated by the agreement.
guidance.inspection: Match the protected fact to a direct nondisclosure or no-announcement duty, or to a confidential-information definition governed by an applicable nondisclosure duty. A general confidentiality clause about business information does not cover negotiations merely by association.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include each independent direct prohibition and, where relying on a definition route, both the protected-fact definition and its operative nondisclosure rule, preserving consent and compelled-disclosure exceptions.

guidance.when: The agreement expressly states that one or more contractual obligations continue, survive, or remain binding after termination, expiration, completion, abandonment, return, destruction, or another identified ending event.
guidance.inspection: Require an explicit connective between a specified obligation and a post-ending period. A restriction that merely lasts for a stated term, an injunction remedy, continuing enforceability, or language describing conduct during a restriction period does not establish survival after termination.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the surviving obligation, the ending event, all incorporated scope language, and any duration or termination condition; exclude remedies and ordinary term provisions.

guidance.when: The exact hypothesis is supported or opposed through a list branch, governing chapeau, class definition, cross-reference, continuation, or multiple independently operative provisions.
guidance.inspection: After fixing the exact actor, action, object, trigger, and polarity, scan the complete contract for all independent supports and their required connective text. Candidate evidence is only a lead. Include a chapeau or definition only when it makes a cited branch operative, and never substitute a nearby clause about a different action, recipient class, trigger, exception, or hypothesis.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Preserve every independently supporting and redundant operative route, each applicable chapeau, linked continuation, class definition, condition, and exception. Exclude headings, neighboring list items, survival clauses used for return duties, retention clauses used for copy creation, and other merely related text.

guidance.when: The agreement expressly grants or conveys no right, licence, title, ownership, or proprietary interest in Confidential Information or associated intellectual property, or expressly reserves those rights to the disclosing party.
guidance.inspection: Require language about rights, licences, title, ownership, or proprietary interests and match it to the receiving party and protected information. A confidentiality, nondisclosure, copying, or limited-use restriction is not itself a no-rights clause. A residual-use permission is not an affirmative grant of ownership or intellectual-property rights and does not by itself contradict the hypothesis.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include every independently operative ownership, reservation, no-rights, and no-licence provision; exclude mere use restrictions, disclosure restrictions, residual permissions, and unrelated third-party-beneficiary provisions.

guidance.when: An operative exclusion or affirmative clause recognizes information independently developed by or for the receiving party without access to, reference to, use of, or violation involving the disclosed Confidential Information.
guidance.inspection: An applicable exclusion releases independently developed information from confidentiality restrictions and therefore supports the permission hypothesis; it does not oppose it. Require an actual independent-development branch. Prior possession, public availability, a generic exceptions chapeau, non-identification language, or external acquisition is insufficient.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the governing exclusion or permission chapeau and the independent-development branch, plus each separate clause recognizing development of similar information and all proof or independence conditions.

guidance.when: An exclusion or affirmative clause recognizes information becoming available through legitimate means other than the disclosing party, from an external source lacking a confidentiality duty, or through subsequent non-confidential release or availability.
guidance.inspection: Confirm an external acquisition or availability route and preserve any lawful, non-confidential, no-breach, or no-duty condition. This includes broadly worded legitimate means other than the discloser and later non-confidential release; exclude independent internal development, prior possession, and mere permission to negotiate with others.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the governing exclusion chapeau and the complete availability or external-source branch, together with all source-duty and no-breach qualifications.

guidance.when: A law, regulation, subpoena, court order, governmental request, or other legal process triggers a duty to notify the disclosing party before or promptly upon compelled disclosure.
guidance.inspection: Confirm that notice is mandatory, is owed to the disclosing party, and is linked to compelled disclosure of Confidential Information. Preserve qualifications such as legal permission, timing, and opportunity to seek protection. A permission to disclose when legally required without a notice duty is insufficient.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the governing confidentiality or exclusion chapeau when needed, the compelled-disclosure trigger, the notice duty, and any cross-referenced provision that supplies that duty. Include each independent notice route, but not later disclosure mechanics unless independently supporting notice.

guidance.when: The receiving party is prohibited from soliciting for employment, hiring, or initiating employment contact with specified officers, directors, employees, or other representatives of the disclosing party, or is separately barred from an expressly stated solicitation of proxies.
guidance.inspection: Verify the actor, prohibited solicitation action, protected representative or expressly defined solicitation object, duration, and exceptions such as general advertising or unsolicited applicants. Mere communication restrictions, use restrictions, or the appearance of the word solicitation outside an operative prohibition are insufficient.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the actor-and-duration chapeau, every independently operative solicitation branch, the text identifying the protected persons or defined solicitation object, and applicable exceptions.

guidance.when: The agreement affirmatively permits use of Confidential Information itself beyond the agreement's stated purpose, including a broader internal-business permission accompanied by a residuals-for-any-purpose clause.
guidance.inspection: Verify a present broader-use route for the same protected information. A residuals clause limited to unaided memory, standing alone, does not erase a separate operative purpose-only restriction. A purpose-only clause, absence of residual language, or permission merely to perform the stated purpose does not establish contradiction.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the broader-use permission, any residual definition and permission, and every operative purpose-only clause bearing on the same information so their scopes can be compared.

guidance.when: An operative clause requires the receiving party to use Confidential Information solely, only, exclusively, or for no purpose other than the agreement's stated purpose or expressly authorized activities.
guidance.inspection: Match the receiving actor, protected object, mandatory or prohibitory polarity, and permitted purpose. Consent exceptions and defined contractual uses remain within the restriction. Check separately for an applicable present permission to use the same Confidential Information beyond those stated purposes.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the actor-bearing chapeau, every independently operative purpose-only or no-other-use provision, the stated purpose where defined elsewhere, and any exception that changes the permitted-use scope.

guidance.when: An operative return-or-destruction duty applies to Confidential Information and is directly triggered by termination, expiration, rejection, conclusion, ceasing interest, completion, abandonment, transaction closing, or another ending of the covered agreement, project, evaluation, discussions, or relationship.
guidance.inspection: First locate an operative return, delivery, deletion, or destruction verb governing Confidential Information; only then test whether the same clause or an explicit cross-reference supplies the ending event. A survival clause, continuing confidentiality duty, restriction period, remedy, or effective date cannot substitute for the return-or-destruction duty. Closing qualifies only when the clause itself requires delivery at the closing that ends the covered relationship.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the actor-bearing duty, protected object, exact ending-event language, and every operative return or destruction branch. Do not cite survival provisions as evidence of a return duty.

operations.rationale: Cases 290 and 622 show repeated substitution of survival language for a nonexistent return duty, while 613 correctly remained unresolved and 331 and 430 contain actual ending-linked delivery duties. The update makes the operative return/destruction verb a mandatory first gate.

guidance.when: An operative clause presently permits disclosure of Confidential Information to the recipient class asked about by the exact hypothesis.
guidance.inspection: Resolve the class separately for each hypothesis. Employees or internal personnel support employee sharing. Consultants, professional advisers, contractors, employees of contractors, and external agents support third-party sharing. A defined collective class supports a hypothesis only when its incorporated definition contains that hypothesis's class. Employee-only permission does not establish third-party permission, and an external-only class does not establish employee permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the permission or exception chapeau, every definition needed to identify the permitted class, and all need-to-know, purpose, consent, and confidentiality conditions.

operations.rationale: Cases 622 and 613 were missed or ambiguously routed despite operative access for contractor personnel or agents, whereas 187 permits only employees and opposes third-party sharing. The update converts the former null catalog into an exact-class permission inference while preserving class boundaries.

guidance.when: The receiving actor is prohibited from disclosing Confidential Information to every third party, person, or entity, and no presently operative exception covers the recipient class asked about.
guidance.inspection: Match the requested class and prohibitory polarity. A possible future consent or approval is not a present sharing permission. For third-party sharing, an employee-only exception leaves the prohibition opposed; for employee sharing, require that employees are also within the prohibition and lack an applicable employee or duties-based exception.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the actor-bearing prohibition, its protected object, and every proviso or class exception needed to determine whether the requested recipients remain prohibited.

operations.rationale: Case 430's blanket third-party prohibition was incorrectly left unresolved, case 187 confirms that an employee-only exception still opposes external sharing, and cases 490 and 383 demonstrate the corresponding class-specific boundary. The parent lacked an atomic contradiction rule for this recurring polarity.

guidance.when: An operative exclusion or affirmative clause recognizes information developed or created by or for the receiving party independently of the disclosed Confidential Information, including qualifying creation before disclosure.
guidance.inspection: Require an actual development or creation route attributable to the receiving side and preserve any no-access, no-reference, no-use, no-violation, timing, or proof condition. Language stating only that information became known independently, was retained, was previously possessed, was publicly available, or came from an external source does not establish independent development.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the governing exclusion or permission chapeau and the complete development or creation branch, plus each separate clause recognizing similar independent work and all proof conditions.

operations.rationale: Case 613 wrongly treated information merely becoming known independently as development, and case 430 confused retention with development. Case 290 shows that receiver creation before disclosure qualifies but requires both the chapeau and creation branch; 622 supplies the conventional independently-developed route.

guidance.when: The operative definition or identification procedure expressly covers oral or verbal disclosure, or affirmatively covers protected information whether or not reduced to writing.
guidance.inspection: Confirm an affirmative nonwritten disclosure route and any condition that makes it confidential, such as contemporaneous identification or later written confirmation. A subject-matter list, generic reference to information, or ordinary nondisclosure clause without a modality statement is insufficient.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the governing definition or chapeau and the complete oral, verbal, or not-reduced-to-writing branch, including all identification or confirmation conditions.

operations.rationale: Case 430 incorrectly inferred oral coverage from an ordinary confidentiality prohibition, while case 383's operative 'whether or not reduced to writing' formulation was annotated as oral coverage. The update adds that observed nonwritten route without allowing generic breadth to suffice.

guidance.when: An operative duty prohibits disclosure or public announcement of the agreement's existence, negotiations or discussions, a prospective transaction, or the transactions contemplated by the agreement.
guidance.inspection: Treat a no-public-announcement rule concerning transactions contemplated by the agreement as covering the protected transaction fact even if it does not use the word existence. Otherwise require a direct prohibition or a protected-fact definition governed by an applicable nondisclosure duty; general business confidentiality is insufficient.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include every independent direct prohibition and its consent or compelled-disclosure exceptions; for a definition route, include both the protected-fact definition and the operative nondisclosure rule.

operations.rationale: Case 622 missed an express no-announcement clause concerning transactions contemplated by the agreement, while 430 correctly lacked any such rule and cases 92 and 334 show direct existence and negotiation prohibitions. The update makes the contemplated-transaction branch operationally explicit.

guidance.when: An operative clause expressly permits or necessarily authorizes creation of copies for a stated purpose, disclosure route, performance need, or automatic backup process.
guidance.inspection: Require permission tied to copying, reproduction, recording, or an automatic process that creates copies. Permission to disclose, use, retain existing copies, or obtain future consent does not authorize copy creation. A proviso concerning disclosure does not modify a separate copying prohibition unless the grammar or cross-reference expressly applies it to copying.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the actor-bearing chapeau and complete copy authorization, including its purpose conditions. Exclude disclosure-only permissions, consent-only prohibitions, and retention-only clauses.

operations.rationale: Case 92 incorrectly converted a disclosure exception into copying permission, while cases 622, 613, and 334 contain actual necessary-copy or automatic-backup routes. The update requires an express grammatical link to copy creation.

guidance.when: The agreement expressly states that an identified contractual obligation continues, survives, or remains binding after termination, expiration, completion, abandonment, return, destruction, or another identified ending event.
guidance.inspection: Locate both the obligation and an explicit grammatical or cross-referenced connection to the post-ending period. Statements that restrictions are reasonable or necessary, ordinary duration clauses, remedies, enforceability provisions, or conduct during a restriction period do not establish survival.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the surviving obligation, ending event, incorporated scope, and any duration or terminating condition; exclude reasonableness findings, remedies, and ordinary term provisions.

operations.rationale: Case 430 falsely inferred survival from a reasonableness finding, whereas cases 290, 622, and 613 contain explicit survival connectives. The update makes the obligation-to-ending-event connection mandatory.

guidance.when: An operative provision expressly denies or reserves a right, licence, title, ownership, or proprietary interest in Confidential Information or associated intellectual property as against the receiving party.
guidance.inspection: Match the rights object and beneficiary exactly. Limited-use, confidentiality, disclosure, or copying restrictions do not imply a no-rights clause. A permission to use information does not by itself grant ownership or intellectual-property rights, and an unrelated rule about nonparty beneficiaries does not address the receiving party's rights in Confidential Information. Without qualifying rights language, remain unresolved.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include every independently operative ownership, reservation, no-rights, and no-licence provision applying to the protected information; exclude mere conduct restrictions and unrelated beneficiary clauses.

operations.rationale: Case 290 wrongly inferred no rights from a use restriction, and case 430 used an unrelated third-party-beneficiary clause with the wrong polarity. Cases 613 and 92 demonstrate the required express rights language. The update strengthens actor, object, and polarity gating without treating use permissions as ownership grants.

guidance.when: The agreement affirmatively permits the receiving actor to use the same Confidential Information, or a defined subset derived from it, beyond the agreement's stated purposes.
guidance.inspection: Require an operative use authorization and compare its object with every purpose-only restriction. Permission merely to retain copies, prepare records, support taxes, comply with law, or possess archival material is not permission to use Confidential Information beyond purpose. A residuals clause limited to unaided memory must be assessed according to that defined subset rather than silently applied to all Confidential Information.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the broader-use permission, any definition limiting its information object, and every operative purpose-only clause bearing on that same object. Do not use retention evidence as a substitute for use authorization.

operations.rationale: The case 430 response based its contradiction on retention or tax-copy reasoning rather than an operative use grant, while 377 contains an actual broader-use route and 622 separates residuals from the general purpose restriction. The update repairs the action and object boundary while preserving genuine source conflicts.

guidance.when: The exact hypothesis is supported or opposed through an operative branch, governing chapeau, definition, cross-reference, continuation, exception, or multiple independent provisions.
guidance.inspection: Treat candidates only as leads and verify the full contract. Before choosing a relation, identify the exact actor, action, object, trigger, class, polarity, and exceptions. A branch cannot be used without a chapeau or definition on which its operation depends. Before NotMentioned, scan for direct provisions outside the candidates. Reject nearby text concerning a different action, object, class, or trigger.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Preserve every independently supporting and redundant operative route and all text grammatically necessary to make each route operative, including chapeaux, linked definitions, continuations, conditions, exceptions, and incorporated formalities. Exclude merely related clauses and evidence that supports a different hypothesis.

operations.rationale: The observed executions omitted required branches or chapeaux in cases 290 and 613, missed direct full-source provisions in 622, and cited unrelated or wrong-action material in 430 and 92. The update adds a mandatory element-by-element source check while retaining the parent rule to preserve all independent support.

guidance.inspection: Verify the actor, prohibited solicitation action, protected representative or expressly defined solicitation object, duration, and exceptions such as general advertising or unsolicited applicants. Mere communication restrictions, use restrictions, or the appearance of the word solicitation outside an operative prohibition are insufficient.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the actor-and-duration chapeau, every independently operative solicitation branch, the text identifying the protected persons or defined solicitation object, and applicable exceptions.

guidance.when: The agreement affirmatively permits the receiving actor to use the same Confidential Information, or a defined subset derived from it, beyond the agreement's stated purposes.
guidance.inspection: Require an operative use authorization and compare its object with every purpose-only restriction. Permission merely to retain copies, prepare records, support taxes, comply with law, or possess archival material is not permission to use Confidential Information beyond purpose. A residuals clause limited to unaided memory must be assessed according to that defined subset rather than silently applied to all Confidential Information.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the broader-use permission, any definition limiting its information object, and every operative purpose-only clause bearing on that same object. Do not use retention evidence as a substitute for use authorization.

guidance.when: An operative clause requires the receiving party to use Confidential Information solely, only, exclusively, or for no purpose other than the agreement's stated purpose or expressly authorized activities.
guidance.inspection: Match the receiving actor, protected object, mandatory or prohibitory polarity, and permitted purpose. Consent exceptions and defined contractual uses remain within the restriction. Check separately for an applicable present permission to use the same Confidential Information beyond those stated purposes.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the actor-bearing chapeau, every independently operative purpose-only or no-other-use provision, the stated purpose where defined elsewhere, and any exception that changes the permitted-use scope.

guidance.when: The receiving actor is prohibited from disclosing Confidential Information to every third party, person, or entity, and no presently operative exception covers the recipient class asked about.
guidance.inspection: Match the requested class and prohibitory polarity. A possible future consent or approval is not a present sharing permission. For third-party sharing, an employee-only exception leaves the prohibition opposed; for employee sharing, require that employees are also within the prohibition and lack an applicable employee or duties-based exception.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include the actor-bearing prohibition, its protected object, and every proviso or class exception needed to determine whether the requested recipients remain prohibited.
